sentences.text: Operating cash flow compounded at 12.8% a year, from $4.86 billion in FY2016 to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198].
FY2021 operating cash flow jumped 89.1% to $16.1 billion, with REGEN-COV adding 66.4pp, driven by a September 2021 agreement to supply drug product to the U.S. government [D241][F6][D582][P39].
FY2022 operating cash flow then fell 24.3% to $12.2 billion because REGEN-COV net product sales recognized in 2021 did not recur [D292][F7][P33].
Growth has slowed since: the three-year revenue CAGR to FY2025 is 5.6% while operating income shrank at 8.9% a year [D767][D769].
Collaboration revenue reached $7.33 billion in FY2025, 51.1% of revenue, and added 9.0pp to growth [S22][D521][D523].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits rose 33.6% to $5.24 billion, driven by higher Dupixent sales [D591][S52][P9].
Net product sales fell 17.3% and subtracted 9.3pp, as U.S. EYLEA sales dropped 42.4% to $2.75 billion on competition, compounded bevacizumab and the shift to EYLEA HD [D506][D507][D577][S43][P10].
Revenue rose 1.0% in FY2025 but operating costs outgrew it by 4.4pp, so operating income fell 10.3% [D440][D464][D441].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% against net income growth of 2.1%, because the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D444][D442][D459].
FY2023 operating margin of 24.9% is the window low, below the 34.6% median and the 55.7% high of FY2021 [F30][D749][D751][D750].
Of the 3.2pp FY2023 decline, R&D cost 4.7pp while SG&A recovered 2.0pp [D453][D465][D466].
SG&A decreased mainly because of lower charitable contributions to Good Days, a patient assistance organization [D466][P5].
The largest drop was FY2022 at 16.7pp, with SG&A costing 6.0pp on higher headcount and Libtayo commercialization expenses [D305][D319][P34].
Net margin of 31.4% sits 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin because other income reached $1.65 billion; the cited passages do not explain it [F50][F30][X117].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income, while free cash flow of $4.08 billion was 0.91x, against a 0.88x window median [F80][D428][F100][D429][D763].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% is above the 26.4% window median [D425][D757].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898 million, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [D447][F90][D424][D430].
Net cash rose to $16.9 billion from $15.9 billion, 117.7% of revenue, ranking 100th percentile among eight peers whose median is -50.7% [D434][D385][D435][D780][D781].
Buybacks of $3.44 billion plus $370 million of dividends took 93.3% of free cash flow, up from 71.0% in FY2024 [X137][X140][D437][D388].
The diluted share count fell 5.6% to 108.6 million shares [D459][X127].
Return on average equity of 14.9% ranks in the 25th percentile of eight peers, against a 38.7% median [D439][D784][D785].
Operating margin fell four straight years, 30.7pp in total, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, with R&D rising to 40.8% of revenue [R1][F26][F30][D420].
U.S. EYLEA sales fell 42.4% in FY2025, a 14.2pp drag on revenue growth, on competition, compounded bevacizumab and a lower net price [D577][D578][P10].
Other income of $1.65 billion, up from $789 million, helped net income grow 2.1% while operating income fell 10.3% [X117][X116][D442][D441].
Data check: table revenue for FY2018 and FY2019 is recast ($5,145.6 million and $6,557.6 million versus $6,710.8 million and $7,863.4 million first reported) [R2][F3][F4][X3][X4].
FY2018 growth is -12.4% in the table but 14.3% on first-reported figures, so margin and growth comparisons across those years mix presentations [D92][D771].
Operating margin below the FY2025 window low of 24.9% would confirm continued compression, while a rise above it would reverse the trend, in the FY2026 10-K [D749].
U.S. EYLEA HD plus EYLEA sales below FY2025's $4.38 billion would confirm franchise erosion, and above it would reverse it, in the FY2026 10-K [S46].
Buybacks plus dividends above 93.3% of free cash flow would show capital return outrunning cash generation and would draw down net cash of $16.9 billion, in the FY2026 10-K [D437][D434].
